claim: The episode separates speech recognition, model reasoning, and speech generation as replaceable parts of a voice system.
Voice activity detection must distinguish real interruption from noise and short conversational acknowledgements.
When newer speech arrives, the system can ignore the result of an older model call even though the compute cost is already spent.
A supervisor runs at a cadence, reviews conversation state, and reports whether the interaction is on track.
Different supervisors can enforce separate rules or validate extracted information.
The speakers recommend voice evals built from many real conversations rather than isolated prompt tests.
